articleTitle: Dual-Branch and Multi-Scale Information Complementary Network for Hard Exudates Segmentation in Color Fundus Images
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is known as one type of complication of long-term diabetes resulting in severe deterioration of vision, even blindness. Hard exudates (HE) are a type of diabetic macular edema and a prevalent cause of vision impairment for DR patients. Detecting HE is essential for DR diagnosis. Herein, a method for detecting HE with a dual-branch multi-scale approach is proposed. Specifically, the model consists of two branches: the main branch is designed to identify prominent features of the lesions, while the auxiliary branch utilizes a standard encoder and a ResNet50 encoder to identify deep features of the lesions, with two different resolution images serving as their inputs. Considering the variation in sizes and shapes, a multi-scale attention mechanism is integrated into the skip connections of the main branch, enabling the model to segment lesions of different scales. The feature maps finally obtained from both branches are aggregated before reaching the decoder, allowing the capture of contextual information from fundus images. Experiments on the IDRiD, E-Ophtha and DDR datasets show that the Dice of our method reached 74.53%, 68.87% and 59.40%, the IoU reached 59.40%, 52.52% and 42.25%, and the AUC reached 80.58%, 83.88% and 74.79% respectively.

articleTitle: FPGA-Accelerated Semantic Segmentation for Urban Scenes
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: To solve the problem in urban scene semantic segmentation due to complex conditions and vague boundaries, an FPGA-based mining area semantic segmentation algorithm was designed. The model follows an encoder-decoder framework, with ResNet being the encoder and Semantic FPN being the decoder. To accelerate and deploy the FPGA platform, Li norm pruning method was used to compress the ResNet model, and Vitis AI tool to quantify and compile the pruned model. The model can achieve a frame rate of 17.6 FPS on the Xilinx Kria KV260 platform with a power consumption of 6.6W, and the energy efficiency ratio is significantly higher than that on the CPU or GPU platform.

articleTitle: Optimum Design of Dead Time of Magnetic Resonance RF Coil
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: After the end of the RF emission of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) system, it must wait for the residual energy of the energy storage components such as inductors and capacitors in the RF coil to decay to a certain extent before the RF receiving channel can start collecting MRI signals. Otherwise, the oscillation current formed by the energy decay process will cause interference to the MRI signal. The waiting time, which is the dead time, should be as short as possible. Shorten the disconnection time of RF switch in RF transmission channel, and the earlier the transmit coil detuning, the faster the residual energy decay; Increase the equivalent resistance of the RF coil resonant circuit, so that the RF coil is in a high damping state, the energy in the resistance can be quickly consumed, and the RF oscillation attenuation can be accelerated; Design active detuning and passive detuning RF resonant circuit, so that the resonant point frequency quickly deviates from the Larmor frequency, the RF coil enters a rapid detuning state, and the oscillation current can rapidly attenuate. The dead time can be shortened by shortening the disconnection time of the RF switch in the RF transmit channel, increasing the equivalent resistance of the RF coil resonant circuit, and using an actively detuning or passively detuning RF resonant circuit. All of the above schemes are able to shorten the dead time, but the energy release in the rapid attenuation process reduces the intensity of the MRI signal and the quality factor value of the RF coil.

articleTitle: A Few-Shot Learning Based Environmental Microorganism Image Classification Method
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Because of the difficulty of collecting Environmental Microorganisms (EMs) and the limited availability of publicly accessible environmental microbial image datasets, the progress of related scientific research has been hindered. The research of EMs is also in trouble because of the lack of samples. To this end, we establish the EMDS-6 dataset that can be used for deep learning. This dataset includes 21 types of EMs, with each type represented by 40 original images and 40 corresponding Ground Truth images, for a total of 1680 EMs images. Nevertheless, image classification of small EMs datasets on convolutional neural networks continues to yield suboptimal outcomes. In order to further solve the small data problem, we did a study on Few-shot Learning (FSL) on this basis. Furthermore, leveraging self-supervision, our approach enhanced the accuracy to 57.40<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> across 21 EMs classes, demonstrating the potential of FSL and Self-Supervision in the image classification of compact EMs datasets.

articleTitle: YOAM: An Efficient Object Detection Network for Protecting Overhead Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: To ensure the sadety of power transmission lines,monitoring cameras are installed at high altitudes for target detection and recognition, allowing for early warnings of mechanical hazards. Real-time performance and accutacy are critical indicators for evaluating a model. To enhance the accuracy and real-time performance of the YOLOv8 model in detecting and recognizing large targets, distant small targets, and targets in complex backgrounds,this paper proposes a new model called YOAM based on two improvements to YOLOv8. First, a grouped depthwise separable convolution is designed to make the network model more lightweight. Second, an improved attention mechanism is designed based on the channel attention mechanism, allowing the attention mechanism to remain lightweight while focusing more on useful information and suppressing irrelevant feature information. To better test the model's performance, we designed a new dataset. Finally, experiments show that YOAM outperforms the YOLOv5 and YOLOv8 models on the existing test sets, achieving an mAP value of 96.7%. Additionally, on the newly constructed dataset, YOAM successfully detected all targets in the images, while YOLOv5 and YOLOv8 showed cases of missed detections.

articleTitle: An Attention Module Enhanced Deep Convolutional Neural Network for Automatic Hippocampus Segmentation Using MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder linked to hippocampal atrophy, affecting cognitive abilities. Clinically, accurate measurement and abnormal detection of the hippocampus based on MRI images are crucial for the diagnosis of AD. However, it is challenging to segment the hippocampal accurately due to anatomical diversity and the low contrast of brain MRI images. In this study, we proposed an improved U-Net model in both 2D and 3D forms. This model uses attention mechanisms for feature fusion and enhancement, aiming to improve the performance of hippocampus segmentation at the edges and low-contrast regions. The proposed model was evaluated using three diverse metrics on two public datasets. Excellent performance was achieved by the proposed model with a best dice coefficient of 0.9261, a best Jaccard of 0.8624 and a best HD95 of 2.6936. The proposed model has the potential to enhance the accuracy of hippocampal segmentation and provide a computer-aided diagnosis tool for AD detection.

articleTitle: Multi-View Mammography Breast Density Classification by SE-ResNet101
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is among the most frequently tumors in women. Early screening is important in the treatment of BC. Breast density is considered to be closely related to the risk of BC, which has attracted widespread attention from researchers. This study proposes a multi-view SE-ResNet101 model for breast density classification on mammograms from four different views. Compared to original model, proposed model achieved robust classification performance with an accuracy of 0.796, an F1 score of 0.796. The results demonstrated that the model achieved higher accuracy and reliability in breast density classification and was able to provide more effective support for breast cancer assessment.

articleTitle: Aircraft Image Management Based on AI Typical Mainland Zynq
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: In the aircraft management system, the universality of aircraft target detection neural network model compression has been verified for many engineering application conditions such as full-range intelligent maneuvering target recognition in specific areas, long-distance maneuvering target detection, and deep space recognition of non-cooperative targets. A data set suitable for aerospace has been selected to complete variable-scale recognition without basically reducing the accuracy. The model is compressed to one-tenth, and the inference time is controlled at the millisecond level. Using neural network compression and quantization after pruning, a 90% compression rate SSD fixed-point model is achieved to control the resize process and effectively prevent precision dissipation, target loss of lock, and energy consumption expansion. Multi-acceleration IP core parallel computing is deployed on the mainland Zynq series single chip to achieve a peak performance of 1.2TOPS and an mAP value of 0.95, meeting the strict requirements of aerospace vehicles for single-time target recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: Deep Graph Convolutional Neural Network based on Adaptive Sampling and Aggregation Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Graph neural networks learn node embeddings by recursively sampling and aggregating nodes in a graph, while existing methods have a fixed pattern of node sampling and aggregation, and usually only consider direct neighborhood. When sampling high-order neighborhood, it is easy to produce over-smoothing, which affects the model performance and accuracy. Therefore, this paper proposes an adaptive sampling and aggregation deep graph convolutional network (Adaptive Sampling and Aggregation Depth Graph Convolutional Network, ASA-GCN). A sampling strategy based on node importance is designed to adaptively sample high-order neighbors of nodes. Meanwhile, an aggregation strategy based on self-attention mechanism is proposed to adaptively aggregate node information within a given neighborhood. Finally, experimental results on multiple benchmark graph datasets show that the model has superior performance on the node classification task.

articleTitle: An Improved Reversible Data Hiding Scheme Based on Referred Frequencies for a VQ Compressed Index
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Nowadays, we usually compress images before uploading them to social media. However, images on social media can easily be copied, so embedding secret messages in compressed images has become increasingly popular. There are many compression methods, such as Huffman, VQ, ZIP, AMBTC, RAR, JPEG, etc. In this article, we propose an improved data hiding in VQ compression method to achieve better capacity and high quality. Experimental results show that our data-hiding approach is practical.

articleTitle: Myocardial Segmentation of 2D Echocardiography Based on the Improved Self-Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: The measurement of different clinical indicators, such as the myocardial wall's thickness and the ventricle's volume, depends on accurately segmenting the left ventricle in 2D echocardiography. This segmentation is essential for making various clinical decisions, such as whether surgery is necessary. However, segmenting the myocardium requires clinical expertise and makes accurate segmenting time-consuming due to the poor quality of echocardiograms. It is essential to develop an automatic myocardial segmentation method. Some deep learning methods, especially the U-net structure, were proposed to support the automatic myocardium segmentation in echocardiography. The model must simultaneously capture the local and global dependency relationships in the ultrasound images for myocardial segmentation in echocardiography. Given the inherent attribute of local operation of convolution operations, this poses significant limitations for U-Net based on the traditional CNN as the basic architecture. For example, when dealing with complex myocardial textures and structures, we need to accurately identify the myocardium's global morphological features and overall structural patterns. Moreover, this locality may lead to deviations and errors when segmenting the boundary regions or the myocardial parts closely related to the surrounding tissues. Our primary focus will be redefining the skip connection using the attention mechanism. More integrated attention mechanisms can further enhance the segmentation effect of myocardial in echocardiography. Therefore, we integrated the cross-attention mechanism when concatenating features in the skip connection. Through conducting rigorous ablation studies on multiple echocardiography segmentation datasets, the performance of the proposed mechanism was proven.

articleTitle: An Efficient Lightweight Network for Breast Cancer Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Image segmentation is widely used in breast can-cer treatment by rapidly localizing lesions. Most segmentation strategies are both time-consuming and labor-intensive, creating an urgent need for an automatic lesion segmentation algorithm to assist ultrasound physicians. CNN-based computer-aided segmentation methods have achieved remarkable effects, particularly with the U-Net series of networks. However, existing methods improve segmentation accuracy by increasing compu-tational complexity, which creates challenges for deployment on ultrasound examination machines with limited computational re-sources. The proposed Convolutional Block Attention Distillation U-Net (CBADUNet) in this paper integrates a Convolutional Block Attention Distillation Block (CBADB) and employs multi-branch deep supervision (MBDS). CBADB integrates attention mechanisms and feature distillation to extract discriminative semantic information from low-frequency features during the encoder stage. This ensures that the nuances and details captured are accurately represented and integrated during the forward propagation, enhancing the overall fidelity and precision of the output. Meanwhile, MBDS utilizes multiple auxiliary branches to adaptively integrate features both the encoder and decoder. These auxiliary branches, which are discarded during the inference stage, effectively facilitate information fusion without increasing parameters. The results from the Breast Ultrasound Imaging (BUS I) dataset indicate that the proposed CBADUNet provides a better trade-off compared to advanced medical image segmen-tation methods, balancing enhanced performance with reduced model complexity.

articleTitle: U-Shape Swin-Convs Transformer for Underwater Image Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Due to the scattering and attenuation of light into the water, the underwater image usually appears with color distortion, blurred details, and low contrast. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel end-to-end model based on convolutional neural networks and attention mechanisms for underwater image enhancement. Specifically, to overcome the limited long-distance dependency capability of the U-shaped structure based on pure convolutional networks, an attention mechanism is embedded into the U-shaped structure to improve the network's ability to capture global dependencies. To reinforce the network's attention to the color channels and space areas with more serious attenuation, a new U-shaped structure is constructed through integrating with a Hybrid Channel Transformer with Multi-scale Feature Fusion module specially designed for underwater image enhancement task. Extensive experiments using the Underwater Image Enhancement Benchmark, Large Scale Underwater Image Dataset and Stereo Quantitative Underwater Image Dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: An Application of Multi-Level Global Attention Framework for Retinal Vessel Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Accurate segmentation of retinal vessels is vital for clinical diagnosis, yet challenges like complex vascular structures, noise, and low contrast persist. While deep learning has enhanced segmentation through contextual feature extraction, issues such as information loss and limited detail representation remain. To this end, we introduce an application of Dense Attention U-Net model with a multi-level global attention mechanism for retinal vessel image segmentation. Experiments on three public datasets show our model outperforms existing methods, achieving F1 scores over 82% and demonstrating its effectiveness in retinal vessel segmentation.

articleTitle: Classification of Cashew Nut Pests and Diseases Based on EfficientNetv2-S
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Cashew kernel has rich nutritional value, cashew shell has very high industrial value, cashew shell is rich in cashew shell oil has high economic value of natural resources. However, cashews are suffering from pests and diseases, resulting in reduced production. Therefore, testing for cashew diseases and pests is crucial to avoid cashew loss. In this study, deep learning model and machine learning model were combined to detect cashew leaf pests and diseases, feature extraction was performed using EfficientNetv2-S, and classification was performed by XGBoost classifier. The visualization technology Grad-CAM was used to generate heat maps for the final convolutional layer of the feature extraction model, analyze the less concerned part of the feature extraction model, and further modify the feature extraction model. In our research, a public dataset is used, and the data enhancement operation is carried out on the basis of this dataset. The presented classification algorithm was tested on this data set. The results indicate that the algorithm achieves high accuracy in the object detection task.

articleTitle: A Movie Role Based Video Dataset for Autism Spectrum Disorder Micro-Expression Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a developmental neurodevelopmental disorder in which patients often suffer from social difficulties, language and communication disorders. Cinemetrics refers to the quantitative analysis and measurement of movies using a variety of metrics. Micro-expressions are very brief, imperceptible changes in facial expression, and the micro-expressions of people with autism spectrum disorders are often a true reflection of their internal state. Therefore, the use of the Cinemetrics method for extracting micro-expressions from ASD patients in movies and analyzing them can help doctors in the early diagnosis of ASD patients. In this paper, a dataset of micro-expressions of ASD patients in movies is established, and 2,944 micro-expression images from 972 shots in ten films are collected and labelled with micro-expressions. Five target detection algorithms are used to detect them. Finally, our database is proved to be effective by the detection results.

articleTitle: Person Re-Identification Approach Utilizing Multi-Scale Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: To address the issue of feature loss in existing person re-identification methods, This paper presents a person Re-Identification network leveraging multi-scale feature fusion. Specifically, a multi-level scale information fusion module is proposed, utilizing the hierarchical structure of deep convolutional networks for fusion learning. This method allows the model to capture information at various scales from different network layer outputs, thereby enhancing the richness and representational power of the features. Additionally, an attention module is employed to refine the fused features, capturing both the essential and detailed features of pedestrians, thereby improving the model's capability to distinguish between pedestrian identities. This attention module can adaptively allocate the importance of features, increasing the network's focus on significant features, and thus improving recognition accuracy. Finally, the experimental results indicate that our method significantly improves the recognition performance of the model.achieving mAP and Rank-1 scores of 88.7% and 95.6% on the Market-1501 dataset, and 77.1% and 87.2% on the DukeMCMT-reID dataset, respectively.

articleTitle: Model Pruning for Infrared-Visible Image Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Infrared-visible image fusion combines complementary information from both modalities, enhancing scene perception in applications such as surveillance and autonomous driving. However, existing deep learning-based methods are often computationally expensive. Our approach involves training an over-parameterized fusion network, applying structured pruning to reduce model complexity, and fine-tuning the pruned model to maintain performance. The pruning process leverages the L2-norm of the Restormer blocks, ensuring that less critical components are removed while preserving essential fusion quality. Experiments on the benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves high fusion quality with significantly reduced computational costs. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of our pruning strategy.

articleTitle: Research and Comparison of Ceramic Image Generation Through Fine-Tuning Stable Diffusion
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: This research explores the effectiveness of fine-tuning the Stable Diffusion model to generate ceramic images. We constructed a ceramic image-text pair dataset to fine-tune the model, to assess the effectiveness of the fine-tuning, We compared the generation results of the fine-tuned model with those of current mainstream generation models(such as DALL-E, Midjourney, and ERNIE-Bot), through both quantitative and qualitative evaluations. The quantitative assessment utilized CLIP Score and FID metrics, while the qualitative evaluation involved scoring and reviews from scholars in the field of ceramics. The experimental results showed that the fine-tuned model demonstrated significant improvements across all metrics, whereas other models exhibited their own advantages in different aspects. Our research provides new insights for applying image generation models in specific fields and offers valuable references for further optimizing model fine-tuning methods.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Bamboo Shoot Segmentation Method Based on Deep Convolutional Network
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: The precise segmentation of bamboo shoots can realize intelligent monitoring of bamboo shoot growth, which is of significant significance to the optimization of bamboo garden production management. This study adopts a lightweight method based on deep convolutional network for bamboo shoot segmentation. First, an experiment was designed to collect images of bamboo shoots in the wild, and a training set and a test set were constructed through manual labeling. Then, the YOLOv8 deep convolutional network model was used as the basic model for bamboo shoot segmentation, and model training and verification were conducted. Finally, this study designed two sets of comparative experiments to effectively verify the accuracy and efficiency of the method. Experimental results show that the detection and segmentation mAP values of the proposed method on the bamboo shoot test set are 0.927 and 0.931 respectively, which are 0.1% and 0.4% higher than the YOLOv8_x network respectively. In addition, the FPS, params and Model_Size of this method are 169, 43.8MB and 92.3MB respectively, which are 51, 24.6MB and 51.6MB higher than the YOLOv8_x network respectively. Experimental results show that this method has high accuracy and real-time performance in bamboo shoot segmentation, and provides important technical support for bamboo orchard production management.

articleTitle: The Possibility of AI-Derived Remote Sensing Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Most of the cases of AI-derived remote sensing analysis are static or quasi-dynamic at most. The discussion in this letter seeks to prove the feasibility of purely deep learning (AI)-derived remote sensing simulation, and a dual purpose Hopfiled Neural Network (HNN) was proposed to this end. Our preliminary findings indicate a satisfactory recording of accuracy, with the averaged Kappa above 0.7 and FOM above 0.8.

articleTitle: Improved Transunet's Segmentation Study of Bone Scintigraphy Lesions
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of irregular targets and fuzzy boundaries in bone scintigraphy segmentation, an improved TransUNet model was proposed. The feature extraction part of the encoder is replaced with an asymmetric convolution residual module to enhance feature capture in different directions and avoid gradient vanishing. At the same time, the cross-fusion module is used to replace the jump connection, which strengthens the deep connection between the encoder and the decoder, suppresses redundant information and improves fine-grained feature capture. In addition, the maximization decision-making method in the two-channel output dimension is used to improve the richness of classification information, capture the uncertain region and reduce the influence of class imbalance in the case of fuzzy boundaries, and obtain a segmentation graph. Experimental results show that the improved Transunet segmentation algorithm has improved the Intersection over Union (IoU), DSC coefficient (Dice Similarity Cofficient), pixel accuracy (CPA) and recall rate (Recall), reaching 0.498, 0.667, 0.662 and 0.761, respectively, which is better than the current mainstream segmentation algorithms. It has certain practical application value.

articleTitle: RS-YOLO: A YOLO-Based Method for Small Object Detection in Remote Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: This paper introduces RS-YOLO, a novel model for small object detection in remote sensing, designed to address the challenges of missed and false detections in scenarios with densely distributed, small objects. By integrating the Biformer, a dynamic sparse attention mechanism with low computational cost, the model can better suppress background noise and enhance the ability to detect small objects. We also utilize an efficient neck structure, Gold-YOLO, based on the Gather-and-Distribute (GD) mechanism to enhance feature fusion capabilities. Furthermore, we combine Inner-IoU and CloU loss functions as a new bounding box regression (BBR) loss function, enhancing localization performance and model robustness while accelerating training. On AI-TOD and DIOR datasets, RS-YOLO achieves mAPO.5 scores of 56.3 % and 74.2 %, outperforming baseline models and other mainstream algorithms.

articleTitle: Entity-Enhanced Question Representation for Knowledge-Based Visual Question Answering
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: A good knowledge-based visual question answering (KB-VQA) model requires detailed visual information, semantically clear questions, and relevant external knowledge to address open visual question answering tasks. Although the significant achievements have been made in current KB-VQA works, there are the following challenges: 1) The presence of entities with unclear referents in the question, leading to ambiguity or unclear descriptions. 2) For generative large language models (LLM), the extraction of information from images is insufficient and lacks critical, targeted details. To overcome these challenges, an entity-enhanced question representation for knowledge-based visual question answering model is proposed. Specifically, 1) We employ natural language processing technique to extract entities from the original question and generate related questions focused on these entities. These questions are answered using information from the corresponding image, and the resulting entity-related question-answer pairs are then utilized to enrich the semantics of the original question. 2) We utilize visual language model to enhance image semantics by detecting labels in images based on the MSCOCO dataset label set, while extracting question-guided image descriptions to better represent image semantics. Finally, we apply in-context learning method to generate the final answer using the frozen LLM. Extensive experiments are performed on the OKVQA dataset and achieve superior performance of 61.59% accuracy.

articleTitle: Lightweight Vit-Based Pedestrian Multi-Object Detection in Building Construction Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: In the construction environment, significant safety hazards and pressing safety detection requirements are evident. Multi-target detection technology plays a pivotal role in ensuring real-time monitoring of safety and regulatory compliance at construction sites. Nevertheless, the intricate nature of the construction environment, characterized by cluttered backgrounds, diverse personnel, and challenging equipment deployment conditions, poses formidable challenges to the efficacy of multi-target detection algorithms. To address these obstacles, we propose a detection methodology that integrates lightweight Vision Transformer (ViT) and lightweight Feature Pyramid Network (FPN). The Lite Vision Transformer (LVT) is a streamlined backbone network that effectively reduces network parameters while maintaining high detection accuracy by optimizing convolutional self-attention and recursive atrous self-attention mechanisms. Additionally, the Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) utilizes spatial multi-scale feature maps to enhance target detection precision. This approach excels in multi-scale target detection and identifying obscured objects, making it suitable for deployment in resource-constrained construction sites. Experimental assessments conducted on the COCO dataset reveal that our method reduces parameter count by approximately 60% compared to the YoloV3-Tiny model while improving accuracy by roughly 5% over traditional lightweight CNN networks.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Seismic Fault Identification Method Based on an Improved U-Net Model
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Seismic fault identification is a core foundation of seismic data research and is crucial for oil and gas exploration. Traditional methods rely on seismic attribute analysis, which are inefficient and sensitive to noise. In recent years, deep learning-based fault identification methods have made significant breakthroughs, but when applied to complex seismic data, the identified faults remain coarse and unclear. To address this issue, this paper proposes an improved Multi-Scale Dilated Attention Dual-Path U-Net (MDADU-Net) model. The model utilizes multiscale convolutional extraction unit to identify fault features of different scales and incorporates dilated attention unit to capture both global information and local details. Additionally, a spatial aggregation gate is integrated into the skip connections, further enhancing the model's adaptability to real seismic data. Experimental results show that the accuracy of the proposed model on synthetic data validation sets improves by 5.28 percentage points compared to the baseline model. Testing on the Netherlands F3 block further validates the generalization capability of MDADU-Net under complex conditions, providing more precise fault identification results for oil and gas exploration.

articleTitle: Image Fusion Algorithm Based on Frequency Enhancement and Shared Tensor Dictionary Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of multi-source imaging technology, image fusion has become crucial in image processing. This technique combines data from various modalities to produce rich fused images for deeper analysis. Existing multi-scale methods often overlook intrinsic correlations between image components. To address this, we propose an image fusion algorithm based on frequency enhancement and shared tensor dictionary learning. This approach learns a shared multidimensional tensor dictionary for sparse representation of components across frequencies and employs a frequency compensation guided filter (FCGF) to enhance high and low-frequency information. Experimental results show that our algorithm demonstrates strong generalizability in multimodal medical image fusion and infrared-visible image fusion, generating higher-quality fused images.

articleTitle: Image Splicing Detection Based on Hybrid CNN-Transformer Network
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Image splicing is widely recognized as the predominant technique in image manipulation. Most current splicing detection methods have low accuracy and poor localization of small-sized splicing areas. Therefore, we design a hybrid CNN-Transformer network for image splicing detection. Firstly, a hybrid structure encoder is constructed, which first uses CNN to extract the input images' local features, and then inputs it to Transformer to calculate long-distance dependencies to obtain global feature representation. Then, a deformable attention enhancement module (DAEM) is designed to make the CNN local features at different scales at each stage more refined and improve the deformation adaptability of the network. Finally, features from the hybrid structured encoder are added to the decoder via skip connections, to make the decoder perform better feature reconstruction. Results on three datasets show that the network can more accurately locate tampered areas and has superior performance than other methods.

articleTitle: Visual Management Based on Integrated Convolution Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Using convolutional neural network technology for model compression, the convolutional layer operation speed is improved through multiple row-column parallel computing units in the convolution operation acceleration module. At the same time, it is proposed that a convolution operation acceleration module should be used to build a multi-way parallel architecture of the convolution layer, saving time and improving management efficiency. By utilizing IP core development and efficient management of algorithm hardware, image big data pre-processing and post-processing calculations are realized through PS-side instruction scheduling. Using a dedicated neural network processor architecture and a dedicated algorithm acceleration core, computing power support is provided, the autonomy of the visual image management system is improved, and the dependence on measurement and control equipment is reduced, thereby realizing the rapid deployment of neural networks.

articleTitle: Intelligent Microbial Growth Monitoring: A Parallel OD600 Detection System Based on Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Microbial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{OD}_{\mathbf{600}}$</tex> measurement is a crucial experimental technique in microbiological and molecular biological research, evaluating microbial growth by measuring optical density at 600 nm wavelength. While convenient, this method has limitations. For instance, different microbial species and growth stages may absorb light differently, potentially leading to biases when measuring multiple strains simultaneously. This paper presents an innovative parallel <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{OD}_{\mathbf{600}}$</tex> detection system capable of simultaneously monitoring growth curves of multiple microbial strains. Our research integrates advanced optical systems, precise mechanical control, and artificial intelligence algorithms, not only improving the accuracy and efficiency of bacterial growth measurements but also achieving parallel processing and analysis of multiple samples. We discuss in detail the hardware design, software architecture, and core algorithms, with particular emphasis on the application of machine learning in multi-strain data analysis and prediction. Experimental results demonstrate that this system significantly outperforms traditional methods in measurement accuracy, automation level, multi-sample processing capability, and data analysis.

articleTitle: The Possibility of Unsupervised and Non-Transferred Deep Learning for Remote Sensing Interpretation
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: We are intended to prove the feasibility of purely unsupervised and non-transferred deep learning technique, as well as its utilization in remotely sensed image processing.

articleTitle: Lane Detection in Complex Scenes Based on Deep Snake
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Aiming at the challenge of lane detection in complex scenes, a lane detection algorithm based on Anchor, LaneSnakeNet, is proposed. This algorithm generates initial lane anchors through clustering and uses ResNet as the backbone to refine lane prediction across different layers on the output feature maps. A detection module LaneSnake based on self-attention mechanism and global feature fusion has been designed, which integrates global information into lane features and is beneficial for regression in covered lanes. In addition, we design a lane shape similarity loss based on prior information of the lane, focusing on the overall constraints of the lane. Finally, experiments were conducted on the Tusimple dataset, and the results show that the proposed algorithm performs well in lane detection in complex scenes, achieving a speed of 135FPS. Compared with the most advanced Anchor-based methods, it maintains competitiveness and faster speed.

articleTitle: FRSK-UNet: Enhanced MRI Brain Tumor Segmentation with Feature Refinement and Selective Kernel Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Accurate feature extraction is essential for identifying tumor boundaries in brain tumor MRI segmentation. This paper introduces FRSK-UNet, a U-shaped network that integrates Selective Kernel Attention (SKA) and a newly designed Feature Refinement Module (FRM). The FRM enhances feature maps by combining channel and spatial attention, improving context and feature fusion, thus enhancing U-Net's ability to segment complex and diverse brain tumor regions. SKA captures multi-scale information through variable-sized convolutional kernels, enhancing the network's comprehension of intricate structures. Evaluated on the BraTS2020 dataset, FRSK-UNet achieved Dice coefficients of 0.8426, 0.8995, and 0.7948, and Hausdorff distances of 1.3516mm, 0.9152mm, and 1.4847mm for WT, TC, and ET regions, respectively. These findings indicate that FRSK-UNet outperforms other leading networks, markedly improving segmentation accuracy.

articleTitle: DHC-YOLO: An Improved YOLOv8 for Lesion Detection in Medical Images*
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Detecting lesions in medical images is challenging due to variability in morphology, size, and boundaries across different diseases. We introduce DHC-YOLO, a novel approach that integrates multi-scale dilated attention, multi-head self-attention, and concatenation within the YOLOv8 framework. This method enhances semantic information aggregation across scales while minimizing redundancy in self-attention without adding computational costs. Our evaluation on brain tumor, colorectal polyp, and esophageal cancer datasets shows DHC-YOLO outperforms baseline YOLOv8 and other state-of-the-art models, achieving <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$mAP_{50}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$mAP_{50:95}$</tex> scores of 88.3 % and 73.5 %, 88.8 % and 67.2 %, and 52.2 % and 21.7 %, respectively. These results highlight the effectiveness of DHC-YOLO for lesion detection.

articleTitle: Lightweight TransUNet Informal Residential Area Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Remote sensing image informal residential area segmentation plays an important role in urban planning, environmental detection, and disaster assessment. With the development of deep learning, the performance of informal residential area extraction has been improved. However, trying to accurately extract the boundaries between different buildings in the same complex is still a challenging task, and at the same time, segmentation model training takes a lot of time. To address the above problems, we propose a deep learning-based segmentation method for remote sensing images of informal residential area instances, aiming to further improve the accuracy of informal residential area segmentation. This paper has the following three main contributions. First, this paper designs and implements a remote sensing image informal residential area instance segmentation method called TransUNet-IRA, which is a model based on TransUNet, and reduces the training file weights by reducing the number of encoder layers and changing the format of the dataset, which increases the computing speed and improves the performance of the model. Second, we combine DiceCE Loss with IoU Loss to form DiceCE-IoU Loss to further improve the model's performance in informal residential area segmentation. Finally, we collect a large amount of meter-level remote sensing image data from Guilin City, Guangxi Province, and Chenzhou City, Hunan Province, and construct a remote sensing image informal residential area instance segmentation dataset for these two regions based on these remote sensing images, which is annotated with three segmentations of the background, informal residential area, and single building in the formal residential area. After experimental validation, our method demonstrates performance advantages on the constructed dataset, not only outperforming classical models such as UNet, ResUNet, AttUNet, and SwinUNet but also improving on the original TransUNet.

articleTitle: Design of an Improved Dish Recognition Algorithm Based on Image Retrieval
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: With the booming of the new retail industry, unmanned billing systems have become the key to improve the operational efficiency of restaurants and reduce labour costs. In the field of payment and billing, traditional recognition systems based on deep neural networks often rely on a single network to achieve the detection and classification of Chinese dishes, but in the face of the increase or decrease in the number of dishes, it is necessary to frequently adjust the type of the network output and re-collect a large amount of image data for training, which leads to high update costs. In this study, a deep learning EfficientNet convolutional neural network combined with image retrieval for dish recognition is used to solve this problem. Firstly, EfficientNet, an advanced dish detection network, is used to accurately locate the positions of multiple dishes in an image, determine their orientations, and effectively separate the dishes from the background. Subsequently, the EfficientNet based feature extraction network calculates the image features of the separated dishes and uses cosine similarity as a metric to efficiently retrieve the dishes in the reference dish library, thus obtaining the classification results of the dishes. Finally, the system outputs the precise location and category information of the dishes. Experimental results show that the EfficientNet and cosine similarity approach achieves an average accuracy of 98.3% on the dish image dataset of China Food Network, which not only significantly shortens the updating time compared with traditional algorithms, but also requires only 1/24 of the amount of image data of the traditional deep learning classification methods. This breakthrough effectively solves the problem of the difficulty and high cost of updating the current dish recognition algorithms. This breakthrough effectively solves the current problem of difficult and costly updating of dish recognition algorithms, and is expected to significantly reduce the cost of updating algorithms, promote their wide application and promotion in the ‘new retail’ catering industry, and better meet the needs of the industry.

articleTitle: Application and Optimization of ResNet Model Based on Spatial Attention Mechanism for Early Diagnosis of Parkinson's Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has been effectively proved for detecting neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson's disease (PD). And the application of deep learning on MRI data has become popular. This study aims to develop a deep residual network (ResNet) that incorporates a Spatial Attention Mechanism (SAM) to enhance the accuracy(ACC) of early Parkinson's disease diagnosis and classification. We utilized the structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) image dataset from the Progress Marker Initiative (PPMI) database, which comprises data from 322 healthy individuals and 287 PD patients. The DICOM images were initially preprocessed, converted to NIfTI format, and aligned to MNI standard space using the FLIRT tool and the DARTEL algorithm. The SPM toolbox in MATLAB facilitated the removal of non-brain tissue and the uniform resizing of images to meet the model's input specifications. Representative median slices were then selected for model input. Our model introduces a spatial attention layer to the traditional ResNet architecture that combines maximum and average pooling to produce a spatial weight map, enhancing key features while suppressing irrelevant information. Experimental results revealed that the ResNet with spatial attention significantly outperformed the baseline model in PD classification, achieving a 96.581% ACC — an 8.547% improvement—and raising the Area Under the Curve (AUC) value varied from 0.94 to 0.97. The model's overall recognition capability has increased with almost unchanged precision, recall, and F1 score. Future work will aim to refine the attention mechanism design to boost the model's generalization capacity and practical utility. These findings are anticipated to offer new insights and technical support for the early diagnosis of neurodegenerative diseases.

articleTitle: Research on Image Recognition Methods Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: In this paper, on the basis of a brief description of deep learning theory, we study the use of image information recognition technology to detect image data, construct training models, and improve the accuracy of image data recognition through model optimization to meet the intelligent needs of daily life.

articleTitle: Visual Perception Inspired Deep Learning Models: A Study of Visual Attention and Information Interaction
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Visual perception inspired deep learning (VPI-DL) is a subset of machine learning, which aims to build new models by imitating visual hierarchy, information-processing mechanism, multi-mechasnism integration, visual specificity and transferability in humans and animals. In this paper, the latest work in the intersection with deep learning, visual perception, and computational neuroscience is reviewed to provide knowledge about the correlation between biological visual perception system and deep learning. First, the cutting-edge researches of VPI-DL models are reviewed and analyzed in the areas of visual attention mechanism and information-processing mechanism. Then, based on the analysis of the above results, some points of view about the prospects of the VPI-DL are presented. Although there are various visual perception inspired deep learning methods (VPI-DLMs), most of them only focus on the local, single mechanism or structure of visual perception, the study of VPI-DLMs remains fragmented. This survey will provide a comprehensive reference for future research in this promising direction. It aims to provide knowledge and insights into visual perception inspired intelligent models and attract more attention to this field from the scientific communities of artificial intelligence and computational neurosciences.

articleTitle: Laser Spots Array Detection for Structured-Light Endoscope
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: In the industrial field, endoscopes are widely used in various detection and measurement tasks, among which laser array structured light endoscopes are key tools, particularly suitable for precision detection and high-precision measurement of complex structures to ensure quality control and troubleshooting in the production process. This study proposes a technique for detecting and identifying spots in structured light arrays during operation. This technology can utilize epipolar information to achieve sub-pixel level positioning, spot array sorting, and comprehensive evaluation of spot quality by calculating five indicators of clarity, relative brightness, information entropy, Gaussian fitting positioning center deviation, and Gaussian ellipse distribution variance of EWM and topsis in working conditions. This technology aims to comprehensively improve the detection efficiency and positioning accuracy of structured light cameras, not only enhancing the camera's positioning capability, but also significantly improving the accuracy and reliability of measurements, ensuring stable and efficient execution of precision detection tasks in complex industrial environments.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Evolutionary for Object Detection Mobile Architectures Search
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Recently, neural architecture search has achieved great success on classification tasks for mobile devices. The backbone network for object detection is usually obtained on image classification tasks. However, the architecture searched through the classification task is sub-optimal because of the gap between the task of classification and object detection. While work focuses on backbone network architecture search for mobile device object detection is limited, mainly because the backbone always requires expensive ImageNet pre-training. Accordingly, it is necessary to study the approach of network architecture search for mobile device object detection without expensive pre-training. In this work, we propose a backbone network architecture search algorithm which is a kind of evolutionary optimized method based on non-dominated sorting for NAS scenarios. It can quickly search the backbone network architecture within certain computational complexity constraints. It better solves the problem of suboptimal linear combination accuracy and computational cost. The proposed approach can search the backbone networks with different depths, widths, or expansion sizes via a technique of weight mapping, making it possible to apply the architecture search method for mobile device detection tasks more efficiently. In our experiments, we verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach on YoloX-Lite, a lightweight version of the object detection framework. Under similar computational complexity, the accuracy of the backbone network architecture is 2.0% mAP higher than MobileDet. Our improved backbone network can reduce the computational effort while improving the accuracy of the object detection network. To prove its effectiveness, a series of ablation studies have been carried out and the working mechanism has been analyzed in detail.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection Method Based on Semi-Supervised Deep Learning for Internet of Things Traffic
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Today, the Internet of Things (IoT) is developing rapidly, with IoT traffic and attacks increasing sharply, posing a serious threat to the stability and security of IoT systems. In this condition, it is crucial to safeguard the normal operation of IoT systems, while traditional machine learning methods usually require manual selection of features with low anomaly detection rates. To tackle the issue of significant deviation in anomaly detection results caused by the imbalance of data samples in IoT traffic, an IoT traffic anomaly detection model (DCGAN-BiGRU) was proposed. Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks (DCGAN) were utilized to learn the inherent feature distribution of known attack sample data for the generation of new attack samples. Therefore, the disadvantage of unbalanced data samples was overcome and the training stability was improved. Bi-Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) consists of two stacked GRU layers. Then the ability of the model to learn more complex patterns in the sequential data was enhanced. The CICIDS2018 and the CICIoT2023 datasets were used as experimental samples to evaluate the model. The DCGAN-BiGRU intrusion detection model enhanced the efficiency and precision of traffic anomaly detection when compared to traditional methods.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Vespa Velutina Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Vespa velutina, an invasive insect introduced to Europe from Asia, is the primary predator of honeybees, significantly contributing to the decline of their populations. Additionally, Vespa velutina has become a considerable threat to human health, as its sting can be lethal to individuals with allergies. The invasion of Vespa velutina disrupts ecosystems by threatening biodiversity and preventing pollination processes, and it also incurs socioeconomic costs, including negative impacts on apiculture and associated management expenses. To address these challenges, it is essential to develop fast and user-friendly automatic identification tools for Vespa velutina. This study proposes to design an artificial intelligence model capable of recognizing and identifying Vespa velutina among various insects. Such a model would enable the creation of devices that can automatically transmit images and geolocations in real-time, thereby enhancing the response efficiency of relevant authorities. The results of this work demonstrate the feasibility of accurately recognizing Vespa velutina using artificial intelligence technology, which supports the implementation of automated systems that slow the spread of this invasive species and protect the beekeeping ecosystem.

articleTitle: Research on Automatic Classification Methods for Tibetan Medicine Urine Diagnosis Images
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Machine Vision, Image Processing & Imaging Technology (MVIPIT)
abstract: Tibetan medicine, one of the four major traditional medical systems in the world, employs urine diagnosis as a unique and widely used method for disease identification in Tibetan medicine. This study developed a joint classification model that leverages deep neural networks to classify the features and attributes of images of urine used in Tibetan medicine. Tested on a dataset collected in real-world conditions, the model demonstrated a classification accuracy of up to 93.6%, laying a solid foundation for the future development of decision-support platforms specifically designed for urine diagnosis in Tibetan medicine.
